title: Notes et dessins sur la generation et le mecanisme des fonctions intimes
shelf_note: No tradition set; collections are the source ones (getty, americana). A 1901 Rouveyre facsimile of Leonardo's Windsor anatomical leaves belongs in a library of early modern science. The `language: Italian` field describes Leonardo's leaves; the printed matter on these pages is French.
structure_note: The run is a blank verso, a pasted printed label ('Feuillet n° 13. . . Verso.'), and another blank: normal for a facsimile portfolio with interleaved guard sheets. The 3 printed backsteps / 1 repeat among only 8 numbered pages are almost certainly these leaf labels ('Feuillet n° N Recto/Verso') read as page numbers, not a disorder. Images 88 and 90 look alike (same stain pattern low on the sheet) but the files differ in size and blank versos of adjacent guard sheets would look like this; I cannot tell a duplicate scan from the images. The counter field pages_translated=46 disagrees with 98 page records carrying a translation (stale counter; many of the 98 are the system 'Blank page' string).

title: Positiones Inaugurales De Altero Tanto … Praeside … Ortholpho Fomanno … proponit … Johannes Christophorus Aveman Isennacensis
shelf_note: No tradition set; collection is the source one (europeanlibraries). A 1635 Jena-type law disputation on alterum tantum (interest not exceeding the principal). It is what the title says; it sits at the edge of the library's subject range (early modern university print, not esoterica or science). Catalogued under the praeses Fomann; the respondent Aveman is in the title only. The stored title is cut off mid-phrase ('Ad diem ').
structure_note: 16 records, all with OCR and translation; signatures A2, A3 on scans 3 and 5 and the theses run 1–9 continuously, so the order is right. The '6' stored as the printed page number of scan 4 is the catchword for thesis 6, not a page number (the pamphlet is unpaginated). Scan 5 includes a strip of the facing page at the left edge.
